title: Quick Ops Bullet List — Dawn Oncall (Marta) 2027-10-15
content:
Dawn shift quick log + followups — keep short, action-first

Date: 2027-10-15
Shift: 06:30–14:30 PT
Primary: Marta Nguyen (me)
Handoff: checked Slack #oncall and #sre-ops; no open major incidents at start

06:50 — Morning checks\- run basic health dashboard checks
  - qps normal; batcher queue depth stable (avg 12)
  - kv-cache hit rate 79% (target >85%) -> note to follow up on small uploads/cold prefixes
  - autoscaler pods healthy (3/3), CPU median 41%

07:15 — Pager: P1 spike on hosted API (INC-2027-1029)
  - Symptom: 95th/99th token latency jumped from 240ms -> ~1.1s for ~18m window (07:02–07:20)
  - Alert: high tail-latency from frontend -> routed to serving-runtime pool a
  - Initial triage: cache-miss ratio at the same time dropped 63% -> increased decoding work on GPUs
  - Quick mitigation: switched route policy to fallback smaller model-variant (routable) at 07:10, tail dropped back to ~260ms
  - Actions taken (commands):
    * scaled dedicated inference pool +2 nodes (kubectl scale deployment/inference-pool-dedicated --replicas=5)
    * forced kv-cache reclaim on edge (curl -XPOST http://kv-cache.internal/admin/reclaim?threshold=0.6)
  - Note: fallback caused small quality regressions — flagged in incident thread

07:40 — Post-mortem notes (scratch)
  - Probable root cause: sudden traffic skew (customer X spike) + local cache eviction due to mem pressure on edge-cache (OOM events in prometheus logs)
  - Hypothesis to validate:
    * Are we evicting aggressively on smaller prefixes? (filter by prefix length)
    * Did a nightly job run and flush caches? Check cron jobs around 06:55–07:05
  - Evidence to collect:
    * edge-cache pod logs (kubectl logs --since=30m) -> save snippets to INC-2027-1029
    * model GPU metrics during 07:00–07:25 (nvtop/gpu exporter)

08:30 — Followups + runbook TODOs (short actionable list)
  - Runbook: add a decision tree for "tail-latency caused by cache miss" (owner: Ravi, due 2027-10-22)
  - Runbook: add command set to gracefully failover to smaller model variant without user-visible quality flags (owner: Marta, due 2027-10-20)
  - Dashboard: add a panel that correlates edge-cache hit-rate + token latency (owner: Celia, due 2027-10-19)
  - Pager rule: lower threshold for cache-hit drop alerts (current threshold 50% -> try 65%) (owner: eng-sre, proposal by 2027-10-18)
  - Post-incident eval: collect 10 sample prompts from affected time window, run evals comparing primary vs fallback variants (owner: PD team, linked to OPS-4123)

09:15 — Smaller items & reminders (notes to self)
  - Revisit autoscaler cooldown config — we saw slow scale-up (5–6m) during spike; consider shorter burst policy for hosted tier
  - Add brief playbook snippet for "forced kv-cache reclaim" explaining side-effects (data staleness risk)
  - File a tech-debt ticket to investigate edge cache memory leaks (start with heap profiles) -> tag SRE + infra

10:00 — Mid-shift check-in
  - No recurring pages after re-route; traffic normalizing
  - Chat with Ravi: he will draft the runbook tree this afternoon
  - Celia will prototype the Grafana panel; asked for a sample query (shared in linked_artifacts)

11:40 — Pager: degraded logs pipeline (INC-2027-1031)
  - Symptoms: dropped log ingestion from prod-apps -> retention alarm; affects alerting for 01:00–11:30 window
  - Quick triage: forwarder pod restarted multiple times (OOMKilled) — upstream backpressure
  - Short-term mitigation: scaled forwarder replicas from 2->4; set throttling on non-critical sources
  - Notes: attach small script to drain backlog for reindex job (scripts/reindex/drain-backlog.sh)
  - Followup: upgrade forwarder memory request from 512Mi -> 1Gi (owner: infra, due 2027-10-18)

12:20 — Lunch pass / TODOs chunk
  - Draft CLI snippet for on-call runbook (copy into confluence when stable)
  - Ping PD about sample prompts for evaluation (OPS-4123)

13:50 — End-of-shift tidy-up
  - Summarize incident notes into INC tickets: added logs and command outputs to INC-2027-1029 and INC-2027-1031
  - Created runbook PR stub: gitlab.com/redwood/docs/ops/runbooks/-/merge_requests/7 (WIP)
  - Flag: need an SLO note for fallback model behavior (product + SRE alignment) -> schedule 30m sync next week

Action checklist (short, 1-line each)
  - [ ] Ravi: write cache-miss decision tree (due 2027-10-22)
  - [ ] Marta: finish fallback-runbook commands (due 2027-10-20)
  - [ ] Celia: Grafana panel + query prototype (due 2027-10-19)
  - [ ] Infra: bump forwarder memory request (ticket OPS-4127, due 2027-10-18)
  - [ ] PD: collect 10 sample prompts & label for eval (link to OPS-4123)
  - [ ] Me: tidy up logs snippets and upload them to the incident (done by EOD 2027-10-16)

Quick commands log (copyable)
  - kubectl -n inference logs deployment/inference-pool-dedicated --since=30m | grep -i oom
  - curl -sS 'https://kv-cache.internal/admin/status' | jq .hit_rate
  - kubectl scale deployment/inference-pool-dedicated --replicas=5
  - curl -XPOST http://kv-cache.internal/admin/reclaim?threshold=0.6

Misc thoughts / questions to follow up (brain dump)\  - Would conservative prefix caching (longer prefix hashes) reduce miss burst? Benchmark idea.\  - Can we add a sticky-routing overlay for high-value customers to avoid sudden cold-cache impact?\  - Validate whether nightly maintenance windows are flushing caches — coordinate with infra cron owners.

End notes: this is messy by design — meant to be a pocket log for handoff. Will clean selected parts into PRs and runbook edits.

Handoff: next oncall (2027-10-15 14:30): Jonas Becker — send this doc and label high-priority followups in #oncall-handoffs

-- Marta
